headline: Fantasy hockey trade suggestions: Guide to the luckiest and unluckiest shooters
take:
Per ESPN, a fantasy hockey guide to the luckiest and unluckiest shooters asks whether hot and cold starts are sustainable and suggests trades to make off the extreme shooting percentages.

Our numbers back the cold side. Expected goals measure the quality of a player's own chances, and so far this season Mark Scheifele has 3 goals against 6.74 expected, with 13 assists and 16 points in 17 games. Juraj Slafkovský sits at 2 goals on 5.66 expected, and Patrick Kane at 1 on 3.12. Scheifele's team takes 52% of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, so the process is sound and goals should come. Slafkovský's 12 points in 16 games with a 30-goal season behind him suggest a similar rebound.

Logan Cooley is the opposite case: 11 goals on 6.01 expected, a gap of nearly 5, so a cooldown is likely. Kane's share is only 35%, so his dip looks more real, and per The Athletic's Mark Lazerus, he isn't expected to play Saturday.
